summary: birch-css-utils ships ~468KB of obfuscated code executed on import under a CSS-utility cover story
details: Package advertises three trivial CSS helper functions (blendTokens, cssVars, memoSize) that require well under 2KB of plain JavaScript. The declared main entry index.mjs is instead a 291KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle (hundreds-of-entry XOR+base64 string array with a rotating dispatcher and _0x-prefixed symbols) carrying a fabricated 'Auto-generated by noelc-css-blender@2.2.1 - token blend cache' header that does not match the advertised API. A 177KB sibling build-cache.mjs listed in files has the same shape and a second fabricated 'Auto-generated by tailwindcss-theme-kit@0.2.0' header, with references to.exit,.search, and Date.now consistent with environment probing. The obfuscated body executes whenever a consumer runs require('birch-css-utils') or import 'birch-css-utils', so any downstream project that depends on this package runs the hidden logic on module load. The combination of a trivial advertised API, ~468KB of obfuscator.io-shaped loader code as main, fabricated cover-story headers, and environment-probing API references is the standard carrier shape for an npm supply-chain loader rather than a CSS utility.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
